product.noRootsDetail: Add a domain and publish its TXT record, or have an admin add an address range. Attack Surface touches nothing before.
product.noRootsPending_one: {{count}} domain waits for its TXT record. Publish it, then verify it under Domains.
product.noRootsPending_other: {{count}} domains wait for their TXT record. Publish them, then verify them under Domains.

changesPage.description: What appeared, went or changed on your internet-facing surface since the scan before. Something new and unexpected is where breaches start.
changesPage.noneDetail: Every scan is compared with the one before; what differs shows here.

assetsPage.description: Every host name under your verified domains that resolves, and every address of your ranges that answers.
assetsPage.noneDetail: Assets show after the first scan of a verified domain or a range.
assetsPage.noServices: No port in the list answered.

exposuresPage.description: What is open that should not be, or is open and set up badly, from what each scan saw. Nothing was tried or sent to find it.
exposuresPage.noneDetail: None of the checks found anything here.
exposuresPage.byPortDetail_one: Across {{count}} asset; the ones that are rarely meant for the internet in red
exposuresPage.byPortDetail_other: Across {{count}} assets; the ones that are rarely meant for the internet in red

certificatesPage.description_one: Every certificate a TLS port presented, once, with where. Warned about from {{count}} day before it ends.
certificatesPage.description_other: Every certificate a TLS port presented, once, with where. Warned about from {{count}} days before it ends.
certificatesPage.subject: Common name
certificatesPage.noneDetail: Certificates show once a scan finds a TLS port.

domainsPage.description: What Attack Surface may scan: domains proven by a TXT record, and address ranges an admin added with a reason. Nothing else is ever touched.
domainsPage.domainsDetail: Each scan reads the TXT record again first. A domain whose record has gone is not scanned until it is back.
domainsPage.addDetail: Attack Surface gives a token to publish in the domain's DNS. Nothing under the domain is touched until the record is found.
domainsPage.name: Name
domainsPage.publish: Publish this record in the domain's DNS:
domainsPage.thenVerify: Then press Verify under Domains. DNS can take a few minutes to show it.
domainsPage.confirmDelete: Delete {{name}}? What was found under it goes too.
domainsPage.noneDetail: Add a domain your organisation owns to start.
domainsPage.rangesDetail: Added by admins only, with a reason kept in the audit log. At most 256 addresses each.
domainsPage.addRangeDetail: Only addresses your organisation holds, such as a provider's allocation in your contract. Your name and reason go to the audit log.
domainsPage.cidrHint: CIDR, such as 203.0.113.0/28; at most a /24.
domainsPage.reasonHint: Why these addresses are your organisation's, 10 to 500 characters.
domainsPage.outsideDetail: Seen on certificates, as CNAME targets and as mail or name servers. Listed only: never resolved or probed.

scansPage.description: Each scan reads the verified domains' DNS and certificate logs, then connects to a short list of ports on what it found.
scansPage.warnings: The last scan went on despite
scansPage.settingsDetail: Set in the environment (ATTACK_SURFACE_*), see the README.
scansPage.never: A TCP connect only, no SYN scan; one TLS handshake and one GET / where they apply. No password, path or payload is ever tried.

auditPage.description: Domains and ranges added, verified, lost and deleted, and scans started by someone. Entries are never changed or removed.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Attack Surface.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Attack Surface, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also add and verify domains, scan and acknowledge changes; admins also add ranges, delete roots, read the audit log, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
